podcast.title: Early Rock Subdivision (Pre-1977)
podcast.body: Progressive rock, referred to as "Prague," was identified as one of the multitude of different directions that rock music had grown into by 1977, signifying an early and distinct subgenre within the broader rock landscape. "Rock had already grown in a multitude of different directions, metal, Prague, psych, and the so-called corporate rock bands like Boston and Kansas."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 2: (90-81)

podcast.title: Presence in Amarok (1990)
podcast.body: The 1990 album "Amarok" by Michael Field includes sections specifically centered on progressive rock. The album is characterized as a complex blend of influences and styles, with progressive rock being one of the key components integrated into its unique, continuous 60-minute structure. "vemos partes centradas en el rock más progresivo."

podcast.title: Baroque and Complex Evolution
podcast.body: Progressive rock, along with psychedelia, transformed rock music into a baroque, complex, elaborate, and sometimes pretentious genre, moving away from its youthful and rebellious origins. "la música roque gracias al roque progresivo y a la psicodelia se convertió en música muy barroca, muy compleja, muy trabajada, muy recargada, a veces incluso un tanto pretenciosa."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Qué es el NO WAVE. Es mucho más que música

podcast.title: Birth, Decline, and 2010s Comeback
podcast.body: Progressive Rock was born in the late 1960s and early 1970s, flourishing as rock musicians became more virtuosic and recording technology advanced, allowing for complex sounds. It fell out of favor when punk and new wave movements criticized it as "too bloated, too inaccessible, too elitist, too complicated." However, it saw a significant comeback in the 2010s, evolving to include styles like Math Rock and Djent, and attracting bands from Biffy Clyro to The Mars Volta and Radiohead. "Prague rock was born in the late 1960s and early 70s, and was a big deal until punk came along and tried to wipe it out." "But in the 2010s, that style of rock saw a comeback."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 4: The Revivals

podcast.title: Characteristics (Early 1970s)
podcast.body: The early 1970s was identified as the "age of Prague Rock," characterized by ultra-complex musical constructions created by "virtual musicians" in sophisticated recording studios. It fused rock and classical music, often being escapist, fantastical, bombastic, and "completely over the top." "The early 70s was the age of Prague Rock, ultra complex constructions made by virtual musicians and super sophisticated recording studios."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt-Rock: Chapter 3

podcast.title: Characteristics and Challenge
podcast.body: Emerging in the late 1960s, progressive rock was characterized by its complexity and difficulty to play, often challenging listeners who preferred simpler, more direct rock music. "It was hard to play, and sometimes challenging listeners who just wanted to rock out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Glam Rock

podcast.title: Contrast with Glam
podcast.body: Progressive rock's characteristic emphasis on musical perfectionism and artists' discretion (e.g., King Crimson) stood in stark contrast to the glam movement, which prioritized spontaneity and flamboyant stage performance. "Y eso contrasta muchísimo con el glam, que era musicalmente más sencillo."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: EL PIONERO DEL GLAM: MARC BOLAN Y T REX

podcast.title: Criticism and Indulgence (Early 1970s)
podcast.body: Despite its complexity, Progressive Rock was not universally accepted and gained a reputation in some circles as "self-indulgent rubbish." This perception, alongside the "cancer of Mellow" and bad AM radio, contributed to a growing frustration that fueled the punk movement. "But Prague Rock was not for everyone in some circles and had a rep of being a well self-indulgent rubbish."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Curved Air was described as a "London-based progressive rock group" which Stuart Copeland played drums for before joining The Police. "Even before he joined Curved Air, the London-based progressive rock group, Stuart Copeland led a unique life, born in Virginia just outside of Washington, D.C. and raised in Cairo."

podcast.title: Decline in Popularity (Late 1970s)
podcast.body: In the second half of the 1970s, progressive rock began to fall out of fashion. While some bands like King Crimson maintained their niche, others like Genesis adapted by evolving their sound. "el roprogresivo fue pasando de moda."

podcast.title: Fantasy Landscape Artwork
podcast.body: Progressive Rock bands like Yes frequently featured illustrations of fantasy landscapes, often painted by artists like Roger Dean, as a distinctive element of their album artwork. "Think back to pretty much any album from Yes, the Prague Rock Band."

podcast.title: Kraftwerk's Influence Questioned
podcast.body: The question is posed whether progressive rock would be the same without Kraftwerk, indicating their significant, albeit perhaps indirect, influence on its development. "Serían lo mismo el rock-proredesivo, el post-punk, o incluso el hip hop?"

podcast.title: Late 1960s UK Dominance
podcast.body: Progressive music, along with psychedelic rock, dominated the UK music scene in the late 1960s. This genre was known for its highly elaborate, meticulously crafted, and perfectionist musical style, often featuring artists who preferred discretion. "la música en el reino nido está dominada por el roxico delico y la música progresiva, era música muy recargada, muy trabajada, muy perfeccionista."

podcast.title: Market Dominance (Mid-1970s)
podcast.body: In 1975, progressive rock was a dominant trend in the music market, with leading bands like King Crimson and Pink Floyd consistently filling stadiums. "Genesis está en el roprogresivo cuando el roprogresivo llena a bastadios, marraffiro King Crimson llena a bastadios, Pin Floyd llena a bastadios, entonces, de aquella seran la música era la tendencia en el mercado."

podcast.body: Field Music's sound is described as a form of rock that is somewhat progressive, including elements of new wave. "es una especie de rock un poco puf tirando progresivo con toques de new wave."

podcast.title: Prized Characteristics
podcast.body: Fans of progressive rock highly valued "lugubrious, intricate, wady" qualities in the music of bands such as Emerson, Lake and Palmer, Yes, Pink Floyd, and Early Genesis. "Lugubrius, intricate, wady. The very things that progressive rock fans prized in the music of ELP, Yes, Pink Floyd and Early Genesis."

podcast.title: Reaction Against Progressive Rock's Pretension
podcast.body: The complexity and perceived pretentiousness of progressive rock directly led to counter-movements like punk and No Wave, which sought to return to simpler, more agile, and rebellious rock roots. "rápido nacieron movimientos que iban en contra de todo esa vertiente, que querían romper con esa filosofía."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Target of Counter-Movement
podcast.body: The emerging pub rock, power pop, post punk, and New Wave movements were deliberately conceived to counteract and oppose these very characteristics, striving for a simpler, more direct sound. "These were what the musicians I'm going to focus on today were trying to counteract."

podcast.title: The Cramps' Abhorrence (Mid-1970s)
podcast.body: In the mid-1970s, Poison Ivy and Lux Interior "abhorred" the progressive rock and singer-songwriter music that filled mainstream record stores, prompting them to seek out rarer, more primitive sounds in second-hand bins. "En esa época estaban llenas de rock, prodecibo y cantáultores, cosa que aborrecían."

podcast.title: Visual Comparison to Funk Albums
podcast.body: Earth Wind & Fire's albums, with their elaborate iconography, were noted to look more like progressive or hard rock albums, sitting comfortably in 70s LP collections next to acts like Led Zeppelin. "They looked more like progressive or hard rock albums, and they sat comfortably in the collections of 70's LP buyers, next to the likes of Led Zeppelin, and yes."
